items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Originally I did have agreements – written agreements with Ahmad Jamal, with Ramsey Lewis.

ctx.x: Tell us about Dakota Staton. You began representing her initially. How did it go?

I started – Dakota Staton was through – I met Dakota Staton through Dave Cavanaugh. It was at his suggestion that I – he said, “Talk to them. They need somebody to represent” – he says, “because I can’t do business with her and talk to her. She needs somebody to be her businessman.” So I talked to her. We came up on an agreement and talked. But I wasn’t that keen on being involved with singers at the time. My thoughts were more like – I – my first

management, I think, was mostly instrumental people. I know it was, definitely, mostly instrumental people: Ahmad Jamal, Ramsey Lewis, and later on Cannonball [Adderley] and people like that. So I was interested more in the instrumental people than I was in any singers.

items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: I did sign up people like Ahmad Jamal, Ramsey Lewis, that was one of the first things.

ctx.x: Okay, well we won’t date you with that.

Remember it all, but anyway, that was my first person to sign up as a manager. And then I said, I was only thinking in terms of musicians anyway. I didn’t know too much about singers and I didn’t, you know that wasn’t my cup of tea was the way I felt about it at that time. So we, I did sign up people like Ahmad Jamal, Ramsey Lewis, that was one of the first things. And by this time George Shearing was on Capitol Records by this time. And that’s a whole other story, how we got on that. I just walked into the…
